<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:8pt"><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center><B><BR>
<BR></B></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center><B>PART I</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<TABLE style="margin-right:48.25pt; font-size:10pt" cellspacing=0><TR><TD valign=top width=73.867><P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>ITEM 1. </B></P>
</TD><TD valign=top width=637.2><P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>BUSINESS.</B></P>
</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We are a provider of global business and financial news, information and insight through newspapers, newswires, magazines, the Internet, indexes, television and radio. &nbsp;In addition to <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> and its international and online editions, we publish the print and online editions of <I>Barron&#146;s</I>, Dow Jones Newswires, Dow Jones Indexes and <I>MarketWatch.com</I>. &nbsp;We also provide news and information of general interest to local communities throughout the U.S. through our Ottaway group of community newspapers. &nbsp;We are co-owner with Reuters Group of Factiva, and with Hearst of <I>SmartMoney. &nbsp;</I>We also provide news content to CNBC television operations and radio stations in the U.S. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We have determined the following three reportable segments based on the manner in which we manage our business: print publishing, electronic publishing and general-interest community newspapers. &nbsp;Over the three years ended December 31, 2005, approximately 56%, 24% and 20% of our revenues have been derived from the print publishing, electronic publishing and community newspapers segments, respectively. &nbsp;In addition, the Company reports certain administrative activities under corporate. &nbsp;Financial information about operating segments and geographic areas is incorporated by reference to Note 13 to the financial statements of this report. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company's principal executive offices are located at 200 Liberty Street, New York, New York, 10281. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company makes available all of its annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and amendments to such reports free of charge through its Internet Web site at <I>www.dowjones.com</I>. &nbsp;These reports are also available on the Securities and Exchange Commission's Internet Web site at <I>www.sec.gov</I>.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Recent Developments</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Effective February 22, 2006, the Company established a new organizational structure pursuant to which it will organize and report its business around its three markets: &nbsp;consumer media, enterprise media, and community media. &nbsp;The Consumer Media Group will include <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> Franchise (including domestic and international print, online, television and radio); <I>Barron&#146;s</I> Franchise (including print, online and conferences); and, MarketWatch Franchise (including online, newsletters, television and radio). &nbsp;The Enterprise Media Group will include Dow Jones Newswires, Dow Jones Licensing Services, Dow Jones Indexes, Dow Jones Financial Information Services, and Dow Jones Reprints and Permissions. &nbsp;The Community Media Group will include the Company&#146;s portfolio of Ottaway community newspaper properties.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>EMPLOYEES</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>At December 31, 2005, the Company employed 7,501 full-time employees compared with 7,143 full-time employees at December 31, 2004 and 6,975 at December 31, 2003. &nbsp;The increase in full-time employees in 2005 was largely the result of acquisitions.</P>
<P style="margin-top:10pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:2.5pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>PRINT PUBLISHING </B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Print publishing, which is largely comprised of the global print editions of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I>, is a leading publisher of business and financial content worldwide. &nbsp;Print publishing also includes our <I>Barron&#146;s</I> weekly financial magazine and our licensing agreement with NBC Universal, whereby Dow Jones provides branding, news content and on-air expertise to CNBC as a further extension of the <I>Dow Jones</I> and <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> brands. &nbsp;The Journal utilizes a global management structure with shared news flows and workforce and a global advertising customer base and pricing. &nbsp;Our overall performance is largely dependent on the operating performance of <I>The</I> <I>Wall Street Journal</I>, which, in turn, is dependent, to a significant extent, on the business-to-business (B2B) advertising attracted by the distinctive demographic profile of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> audience.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><U>U.S. Publications </U></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>The Wall Street Journal</I>, our flagship publication, is one of the country&#146;s largest daily national newspapers with average print circulation of 1,739,000 in 2005. &nbsp;The Journal&#146;s three major national editions are printed at 17 printing plants located throughout the U.S. &nbsp;The Journal also sells regional advertising in 18 regional editions. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>3</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>The Wall Street Journal</I> has an overall daily print capacity of 96 pages, including 24 pages of color. &nbsp;In addition to its business coverage, the Journal also covers the &#147;business of life&#148; with its Personal Journal section which launched in 2002 and runs every Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, its Weekend Journal section, which debuted in 1998 and runs every Friday and includes pages devoted to travel, wine, sports, shopping, residential real estate and the arts, and its Saturday Weekend Edition, which we launched in September 2005. &nbsp;The Journal also publishes special reports at various times of the year on topics such as technology, personal finance and executive compensation, e-commerce and health and medicine, as well as demographically targeted sections devoted to subjects of retirement and small business. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In September 2005, we launched the Weekend Edition of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I>, which was a key element of our long range strategic plan. We expect the Weekend Edition to build off the success of our Weekend Journal and Personal Journal sections in attracting more consumer-oriented advertisers and reduce our reliance over time on B2B financial and technology advertising. &nbsp;The Weekend Edition is delivered to readers at home on the weekend, enabling advertisers to reach readers in the right place at the right time, which is highly conducive to influencing their consumer spending decisions. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In October 2005, we announced a number of innovative design and content enhancements to the Journal's U.S. print edition, which will be made to better serve existing readers and attract new ones. &nbsp;These improvements will include changes to the Journal's organization, navigation and content--as well as stronger links to<I> The Wall Street Journal Online </I>at <I>WSJ.com </I>designed to make accessing Journal content faster and more convenient for readers. &nbsp;Some of these enhancements will be introduced during 2006, culminating in January 2007 with a redesign of the Journal, including reformatting of the Journal to a smaller, more convenient and more industry-standard 48-inch web width from its current 60-inch web width. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Journal production process employs electronic pagination and satellite transmission of page images to outlying printing plants to enable early delivery of fresher content to the majority of our readers. &nbsp;<I>The Wall Street Journal</I> is delivered principally in three ways. Approximately 123,000 copies of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> are sold at newsstands. &nbsp;Most home and office subscription deliveries are handled through our National Delivery Service, Inc. subsidiary which in 2005 provided early morning delivery to about 1.3 million, or 83%, of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I>&#146;s subscribers each publishing day. &nbsp;The balance of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I>&#146;s home and office deliveries is made by second class postal service.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Journal reaches additional readers through <I>The Wall Street Journal Sunday</I>, which focuses on personal finance and careers and is published once a week in the business sections of local newspapers with combined circulation of about 9.1 million in more than 81 community newspapers.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Barron&#146;s</I>, the Dow Jones Business and Financial Weekly, is a weekly magazine with average circulation in 2005 of about 298,000 that caters to financial professionals, individual investors and others interested in financial markets. &nbsp;<I>Barron&#146;s</I> is printed in all of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I>&#146;s 17 printing plants. &nbsp;It is delivered by second-class postal service and through National Delivery Service with about 57,000 newsstand copies sold each week.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>The Wall Street Journal Classroom Edition</I> is published nine times during the school year and is read by an estimated 750,000 students every month during the academic year in more than 5,000 middle school and high school classrooms throughout the U.S. &nbsp;Individuals, organizations and corporations sponsor more than one-third of all subscriptions and schools sponsor the remainder. &nbsp;<I>The Wall Street Journal Campus Edition</I> is included in college newspapers throughout the U.S. and includes the week&#146;s top business news and feature stories.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><U>International Publications </U></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>The Wall Street Journal Europe</I>, which had an average circulation of 88,000 in 2005, is headquartered in Brussels, Belgium and printed in Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. &nbsp;It is available on the day of publication in continental Europe, the United Kingdom, and parts of the Middle East and North Africa. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>The Wall Street Journal Asia</I>, which had an average circulation of 81,000 in 2005, is headquartered in Hong Kong and printed in Hong Kong, Singapore, Japan, Thailand, Malaysia, Taiwan, the Philippines, Korea and Indonesia.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Starting in 2003, the international editions of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> added news and opinion from <I>The Washington Post</I>. &nbsp;In October of 2005, we launched reformatted compact international editions of the Journal in a more convenient and easier to read format and are more tightly integrated with <I>The Wall Street Journal Online at</I> <I>WSJ.com</I> <I>(WSJ.com) </I>to better serve the needs of highly mobile international business leaders. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We also publish <I>The Wall Street Journal Special Editions</I>, which are a collection of Journal pages in local languages distributed as part of 39 newspapers in 40 countries.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>4</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the fourth quarter of 2004, we relaunched the<I> Far Eastern Economic Review</I>, a Hong Kong based newsweekly magazine, as a monthly periodical of issues and ideas largely written by Asian opinion leaders from the fields of politics, business and academics. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>ELECTRONIC PUBLISHING</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Electronic publishing, which electronically distributes business and financial news and information, includes the operations of Dow Jones Newswires, Consumer Electronic Publishing and Dow Jones Indexes/Ventures. &nbsp;Consumer Electronic Publishing includes the results of <I>WSJ.com</I> and its related Web sites, MarketWatch and its related Web sites, and the Company&#146;s licensing and radio/audio businesses. &nbsp;Revenues in the electronic publishing segment, which comprised about 24% of our total revenues over the three years ended in 2005, are mainly subscription-based but also include online advertising and other revenues.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><U><BR></U></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><U>Dow Jones Newswires </U></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Dow Jones Newswires is a premier provider of real-time, comprehensive business news and information for financial professionals around the world. &nbsp;Its news is displayed on approximately 304,000 English-language terminals worldwide providing users with real-time information on equity, fixed income, foreign exchange, commodities and energy markets. &nbsp;Dow Jones Newswires has a dedicated staff of more than 900 journalists in addition to drawing on the global resources of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> and the Associated Press. &nbsp;Newswires also distributes selected portions of its content to the retail customers of on-line brokers. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Dow Jones News Service is North America&#146;s leading source of business and financial news on U.S. and Canadian companies and markets for brokerage firms, banks, investment companies and other businesses. &nbsp;Capital Markets Report covers global debt and money markets. &nbsp;Corporate Filings Alert provides real-time news covering SEC filings, bankruptcy courts and government agencies. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Dow Jones Economic Report and the Dow Jones Financial Wire, which are produced outside the United States, provide international economic, business and financial news to subscribers in 71 countries. &nbsp;In addition to these two broad international newswires, Newswires publishes specialized wires dedicated to the coverage of European and Asian equities, banking and foreign exchange markets as well as the World Equities Report, which serves U.S. institutions investing in international markets. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Dow Jones Newswires also publishes on its own or with local partners, in Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Dutch, Italian, German and Russian. &nbsp;In April 2004, we acquired the remaining interest in the news operations of Vereinigte Wirtschaftsdienste GmbH (VWD), a German local-language news service. &nbsp;Previously, we were a minority shareholder in VWD.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On March 19, 2004, we acquired Alternative Investor Group, a company serving the private equity and venture capital markets with newsletters, conferences and databases. &nbsp;Alternative Investor was integrated with Dow Jones Newswires, its newsletters division and Technologic Partners business, which we acquired in late 2003, to form Dow Jones Financial Information Services. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><U>Consumer Electronic Publishing </U></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>WSJ.com</I>, introduced in 1996, is a paid online subscription site that offers continuously updated coverage of business news both in the U.S. and abroad. &nbsp;<I>WSJ.com</I> content comprises the global resources of <I>The Wall Street Journal </I>and Dow Jones Newswires as well as its own dedicated journalists. &nbsp;In addition to continuously updated exclusive real-time news and scoops, subscribers have access to the full text of each day&#146;s global editions of the Journal, approximately 30,000 in-depth company background reports, an archive of Journal and Dow Jones news articles, and personalized news and stock portfolios. &nbsp;<I>WSJ.com</I> had 768,000 subscribers at the end of 2005 and was the largest paid subscription news site on the Internet.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On January 21, 2005, we completed the acquisition of MarketWatch, a leading provider of business, company and markets news, financial information and analytical tools which also operates two award-winning Web sites: <I>MarketWatch.com</I> and <I>BigCharts.com</I>. &nbsp;These free, advertising-supported Web sites served approximately seven million unique visitors per month with timely market news and information. &nbsp;MarketWatch also operates newsletters, radio and television businesses and the MarketWatch Licensing Services group, which is a leading licensor of market news, data, investment analysis tools and other online applications to financial services firms, media companies, and corporations. &nbsp;We have fully integrated MarketWatch into the Consumer Electronic Publishing business.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>5</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We believe that the MarketWatch acquisition complements <I>The Dow Jones Online Network</I> (which includes <I>WSJ.com </I>and its family of free Web sites, <I>Opinion Journal, Career Journal, Real Estate Journal, Start Up Journal </I>and<I> College Journal</I> as well as the paid <I>Barron&#146;s Online</I> Web site) which provides premium business news to about three million unique visitors per month. &nbsp;By combining the traffic of <I>The Wall Street Journal Online</I> network and MarketWatch into the <I>Dow Jones Online Network</I>, our Web sites averaged approximately nine million unduplicated unique visitors per month during 2005. &nbsp;The licensing businesses of MarketWatch provided additional assets, such as online charting and other tools, which extended the reach of our business-to-business licensing operations. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In January 2006, the Company relaunched <I>Barron&#146;s Online</I>, which previously had been included as part of <I>WSJ.com</I> as a fully stand-alone subscription product. &nbsp;As of late January 2006, the site had more than 45,000 paid subscribers. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Consumer Electronic Publishing also includes our radio/audio business and our consumer electronic licensing division, which offers electronic rights to use Dow Jones content. &nbsp;<I>The Wall Street Journal Radio Network</I> produces and distributes late-breaking business reports during the week to 250 radio stations across the country, covering 93% of the population. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><U>Dow Jones Indexes/Ventures </U></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In 1997, we began licensing the Dow Jones Industrial Averages as well as other indexes as the basis for trading options, futures, unit trusts, annuities, exchange traded funds, mutual funds, derivatives and specialized structured products. &nbsp;Dow Jones Indexes offers more than 5,000 indexes, including a variety of specialty indexes, such as the <I>Dow Jones-AIG Commodity Index</I>, the <I>Dow Jones Select Dividend Index</I> and the <I>Dow Jones Islamic Market Indexes</I>. &nbsp;During 2004, Dow Jones Indexes launched a new family of hedge fund indexes and also partnered with Wilshire Associates to provide the <I>Dow Jones Wilshire</I> index family, which features the <I>Dow Jones Wilshire 5000.</I> </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Dow Jones Ventures includes our reprints/permissions business, which sells print or electronic reprints of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> and <I>Barron&#146;s</I> stories. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>COMMUNITY NEWSPAPERS</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>This segment consists of our wholly-owned Ottaway Newspapers, Inc. subsidiary. &nbsp;Revenues in this segment include subscription, advertising and other revenues. &nbsp;These revenues are largely dependent on local consumer-based advertising revenue and comprised about 20% of our revenues over the past three years.&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Our community newspapers serve relatively small,&nbsp;isolated&nbsp;communities, outside the heavy competitive pressures of large metropolitan papers. &nbsp;In October 2005, we purchased <I>The Barnstable Patriot, </I>a small 5,000 circulation, weekly newspaper. &nbsp;In May 2003, we acquired&nbsp;<I>The Record of Stockton, California, </I>which had daily circulation of about 60,000.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Ottaway publications now include 15 general-interest dailies, published in California, Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Hampshire, New York, Oregon and Pennsylvania. &nbsp;Average 2005 circulation of the dailies was approximately&nbsp;431,000; Sunday circulation was approximately&nbsp;473,000. &nbsp;Ottaway also publishes&nbsp;19 weekly newspapers and 21 other publications. &nbsp;The primary delivery method for the newspapers is by carrier delivery.&nbsp; </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Ottaway has invested in a new content management system for its print and online products. &nbsp;This system will streamline newsroom workflow and allow for the automated transfer of print content to the Web. &nbsp;In addition, this new technology is being incorporated into the segment&#146;s Internet platform, which also includes standardized ad serving, classified verticals, email marketing and new content modules.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Arial; color:#0000FF" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>STRATEGIC ALLIANCES (Included in Equity in Earnings of Associated Companies)</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Factiva</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Dow Jones Reuters Business Interactive LLC (Factiva) is a 50/50 joint venture launched in mid-1999 with Reuters Group Plc. &nbsp;Factiva is the leading provider of current and archived global business and financial news and information to enterprise end users worldwide. &nbsp;In addition to its flagship product, <I>Factiva.com</I>, the company provides customers with content delivery tools and services that customize access to Factiva&#146;s content collection. &nbsp;Factiva's business information sources include exclusive third party access to Dow Jones and Reuters Newswires and <I>The Wall Street Journal</I>, plus nearly 9,000 other sources from around the world. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>6</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>CNBC International</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In December 2005, the Company completed the disposal of its 50% interests in both CNBC Europe and CNBC Asia (collectively CNBC International), as well as its 25% interest in CNBC World, to NBC Universal for nominal consideration pursuant to a July 2005 agreement. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>SmartMoney</I> </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>SmartMoney is a 50/50 joint venture with Hearst Corp. &nbsp;<I>SmartMoney</I> magazine, The Wall Street Journal Magazine of Personal Business, features sections on personal investing, spending and saving money, and has circulation of more than 800,000 copies. &nbsp;SmartMoney also includes <I>SmartMoney.com</I> and SmartMoney Custom Solutions. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Vedomosti</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Vedomosti, a joint venture owned equally by Dow Jones, Pearson plc and Independent Media, was introduced in 1999. &nbsp;Circulation reached 68,000 in 2005, with original content created by 94 local reporters and editors and content from <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> and <I>The Financial Times</I> translated into Russian. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>STOXX, Ltd.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>STOXX, Ltd. is a joint venture owned equally by Dow Jones and the leading stock exchanges of Germany (Deutsche Borse) and Switzerland (Swiss Exchange). &nbsp;STOXX develops, maintains, distributes and markets the Dow&nbsp;Jones STOXX indices.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Other</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Other equity investments include HB-Dow Jones S.A., a part-owner of Economia, a publishing company in the Czech Republic and Adicio, Inc. (formerly known as CareerCast, Inc.), a leading supplier of data services to employers and online career sites. &nbsp;In April 2005, the Company concluded the sale of its 39.9% minority interest in F.F. Soucy Inc., a Canadian newsprint mill, to its majority owner, Brant-Allen Industries, Inc. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:10pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:2.5pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>RAW MATERIALS</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The primary raw material used by the Company is newsprint. &nbsp;In 2005, approximately 215,000 metric tons were consumed. &nbsp;Newsprint was purchased principally from eight suppliers. &nbsp;The Company was a limited partner in F.F. Soucy, Inc. &amp; Partners, L.P., Riviere du Loup, Quebec, Canada until April 2005 as discussed above. &nbsp;F.F. Soucy furnished 16% of total newsprint requirements in 2005. &nbsp;The Company has signed long-term contracts with certain newsprint suppliers, including F.F. Soucy, for a substantial portion of its annual newsprint requirements. &nbsp;For many years the available sources of newsprint have been adequate to supply the Company's needs.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:10pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:2.5pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>COMPETITION</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Dow Jones print publishing businesses compete for readers and advertisers with a wide range of information providers in many different channels of distribution. &nbsp;All national and major metropolitan general interest newspapers and many small city or suburban papers carry business and financial content as do many Internet-based services (see those listed below) as well as television and radio. &nbsp;In addition, specialized magazines in the business and financial field (such as <I>Forbes, Fortune </I>and<I> BusinessWeek)</I>, as well as general news magazines, (such as <I>Time</I> and <I>Newsweek)</I> publish substantial amounts of business-related material. &nbsp;The Journal also competes for advertising with non-business publications offering audiences of similar demographic quality, such as lifestyle magazines (e.g., <I>The New Yorker</I>, <I>Wine Spectator</I> and <I>Gourmet</I>). </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company's newswires compete with other global financial newswires including Reuters Group Plc, Bloomberg L.P. and other organizations that publish financial news as well as many internet-based providers of financial news and information. &nbsp;The Company's newswires maintain a stronger market position in North America than internationally. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Consumer Electronic Publishing competes with other Web sites that offer continuously updated coverage of business news as well as licensing of electronic content. &nbsp;Unlike <I>WSJ.com</I>, competitors do not, for the most part, utilize a full online paid subscription model, and most remain free sites. &nbsp;Competitors include <I>FT.com</I>, <I>New York Times Digital</I>, <I>TheStreet.com</I>, Bloomberg, <I>Forbes.com</I>, <I>Yahoo!Finance</I>, <I>CNET</I>, <I>CNN Money</I> and <I>MSNMoney/CNBC</I>.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Dow Jones Indexes competes with the indexes distributed by various organizations, including Standard &amp; Poor&#146;s, <I>The Financial Times</I>, and Morgan Stanley Capital International. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Ottaway competes with the metropolitan general-interest newspapers, and other community newspapers as well as Web sites and radio and television stations in their respective local markets.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Factiva competes with various business information service providers, including Dialog Corporation and Lexis-Nexis. &nbsp;Factiva also competes with various internet-based information search services such as Google, Microsoft and Yahoo!.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>7</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<TABLE style="margin-right:48.25pt; font-size:10pt" cellspacing=0><TR><TD valign=top width=73.867><P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>ITEM 1A.</B></P>
</TD><TD valign=top width=637.2><P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>RISK FACTORS.</B></P>
</TD></TR>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<A NAME="_Toc94466822"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Forward-looking statements</B></P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>By their nature, forward-looking statements involve risk and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from anticipated results. &nbsp;Such risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to: </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Risks Relating to Our Business</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Advertising revenues</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We derive a majority of our revenue from advertising, primarily in connection with our print publications and Web sites. &nbsp;Our overall performance is largely dependent on the operating performance of <I>The</I> <I>Wall Street Journal</I> (including its international and online editions), which, to a significant extent, is dependent upon business-to-business (&#147;B2B&#148;) advertising attracted by the distinctive demographic profile of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> audience.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Our advertising revenues are impacted by economic and competitive changes in any of our advertising markets, but particularly in our core B2B market. &nbsp;We continue to experience depressed levels of B2B advertising, especially in technology and finance, which have typically represented approximately 40% of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I>&#146;s advertising linage. These categories may or may not return to historical levels. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Although we have taken initiatives (including the 2002 introduction of our Personal Journal section of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> and our new Weekend Edition launched in September 2005) to attract more consumer advertising and other diversified advertising, we may or may not be able to further penetrate these new consumer advertising segments. &nbsp;In particular, The Wall Street Journal&#146;s broad national circulation limits our ability to provide certain local advertising to consumers. &nbsp;Furthermore, our new Weekend Edition may fail to generate anticipated advertising revenues, resulting in greater losses than are currently expected in its first two years of operation. &nbsp;In addition, the new Weekend Edition may draw advertising away from our other consumer advertising sections, such as the Friday Weekend Journal section of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> (introduced in 1998) and Personal Journal, for consumer advertising revenues. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Our ability to attract advertisers to our Web sites depends on our ability to generate traffic to our Web sites and the rate at which users click through on advertisements. &nbsp;Advertising revenues from our Web sites may be negatively impacted by fluctuations or decreases in our traffic levels. &nbsp;In addition, we rely on establishing and maintaining distribution relationships with high-traffic Web sites for a portion of our traffic, for which we pay fees, and we could be adversely effected by any changes in such relationships.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Our community newspapers rely on advertising revenue from local advertisers. &nbsp;These revenues may be negatively impacted by the condition of the economy in the areas where our community newspapers are circulated and by the advertising habits of large regional advertisers who may change their spending patterns or go out of business.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR>
<BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>8</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Circulation revenues</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Both advertising and circulation revenue are impacted by circulation and readership levels. &nbsp;The distinctive demographics of The Wall Street Journal's circulation and readership base (in particular, its influential and affluent audience that makes significant B2B spending decisions and spends heavily on consumer items) is an important factor in generating circulation and advertising revenues. &nbsp;Print circulation and readership at <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> and Ottaway &#150; and the print publishing industry overall &#150; are subject to competition and in particular are being negatively impacted by the preferences of some consumers to receive all or a portion of their news in new media formats and from sources other than traditional newspapers, and the proliferation of these new media formats and sources. &nbsp;The risk exists that this trend may continue or that our circulation or readership may be negatively impacted by changes made from time to time by agencies such as the Audit Bureau of Circulations and various syndicated research organizations in the way they measure circulation and readership numbers. &nbsp;While we seek to maintain our print circulation base, we may not be successful in doing so or may incur significant additional costs in attempting to do so and we may not be able to recover these costs through increased circulation and advertising revenues. &nbsp;If we cannot maintain our print circulation and readership base, this could, in turn, adversely affect our circulation revenues and advertising revenues by reducing the willingness of advertisers to place print ads with us and/or the rates they are willing to pay. &nbsp;While at the same time this trend is positively impacting our &#150; and others&#146; -- online businesses, online is relatively smaller than print so the positive impact of this trend may not offset the negative impact on our print profitability.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Subscriptions; Licensing</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Certain of our electronic publishing businesses, including Dow Jones Newswires, are subscriber-based and are vulnerable to losses in the number of subscribers. &nbsp;For example, Dow Jones Newswires could lose subscriptions, measured by the number of terminals carrying Dow Jones Newswires, as a result of business consolidations and layoffs in the financial services industry. &nbsp;Similarly, <I>WSJ.com</I>, which currently is the largest paid subscription news site on the Internet, may not be able to continue to increase revenues through growing the number of subscribers. &nbsp;Unlike <I>WSJ.com</I>, our competitors do not, for the most part, utilize a full online paid subscription model, and most remain free Web sites. &nbsp;Other of our electronic publishing businesses, including Dow Jones Indexes and MarketWatch Licensing Services, rely on revenues from licensing our products and content to third-parties. &nbsp;Licensing revenues depend on new customer contracts and customer contract renewals, and could decrease if we do not generate new licensing business or existing customers renew for lesser amounts, terminate early or forego renewal. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Arial" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Seasonality</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Our results of operations are subject to seasonal fluctuations, which typically cause revenues in the third quarter (which includes the months of July and August) to be lower than revenues in the remainder of the year.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Cost structure</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We have done much cost-cutting over the last several years, but future cost control efforts may not be as successful as anticipated and we may not be able to continue limiting our expense growth. &nbsp;Factors that may impact our ability to control expense growth in the future include our prior cost cutting, the tightening of the labor market and the resulting risk of loss of key employees, and our recent growth initiatives, such as the MarketWatch acquisition and the new Weekend Edition, and future growth initiatives. &nbsp;If we are unable to continue to control expense growth in the future, there may be an adverse effect on our overall profitability.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Competition</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>All of our products and services face intense competition from other newspapers, national business magazines, television, trade publications, newsletters, research reports and services, free and paid Internet sites, other new media and other forms of corporate marketing. &nbsp;We compete for advertising revenues, subscriptions and consumers, which include readers, online users and television viewers. &nbsp;Metropolitan general interest newspapers and many small city or suburban papers carry business and financial content, as do many Internet-based services as well as television and radio. &nbsp;In addition, specialized magazines in the business and financial field, as well as general news magazines, publish substantial amounts of business-related material. &nbsp;<I>The Wall Street Journal</I> also competes for advertising with non-business publications offering audiences of high demographic quality, such as technology and lifestyle magazines. &nbsp;Circulation revenues at our community newspapers may be negatively impacted by local competition, including free publications. &nbsp;Nearly all of these other publications and services seek audiences and seek to sell advertising, making them competitive with our publications and services and affecting our ability to attract and retain advertisers and consumers. &nbsp;We have experienced declines in advertising that we believe are due to advertisers migrating their campaigns online or to other forms of media and marketing that can reach either more mass consumer audiences or more targeted audiences. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>9</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Our efforts to expand in Europe have been limited by substantial competition from local language publications, other international publications, and local and international television networks, as well as the limited nature of the foreign language market which we serve. &nbsp;In Asia, our presence with our Pan-Asia publications may be threatened by developments within the region such that readers may prefer local language or local market publications. &nbsp;As the economies of the various individual Asian nations develop over time, we may encounter further difficulties in continuing to appeal to a broader Pan-Asian audience. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Our Dow Jones Newswires business and financial news products are distributed through a limited number of vendors, which distribute our news over their platforms into financial services firms that receive our content by way of subscriptions with these vendors. &nbsp;Newswires has entered into a bundling arrangement to deliver a selection of our news on all Moneyline Telerate terminals worldwide; this arrangement is important to Newswires&#146; international revenues and may be adversely affected by the recent acquisition by Reuters of the Moneyline Telerate business. &nbsp;Moreover, sales of our Dow Jones Newswire products may continue to be negatively impacted by technological changes and changes in the brokerage industry, which have resulted in a diminishing reliance on real time news as business and financial news has become increasingly available via Internet-based publications and services. &nbsp;In addition, as we strive to increase our international revenues from the Dow Jones Newswires business, we may not succeed given the competition from and subscribers&#146; desire for, local language news services.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>There can be no assurance that we will be able to increase or to maintain the advertising, readership, circulation or subscriptions market share that we currently enjoy. &nbsp;In addition, changes in the regulatory and technological environment are bringing about a global consolidation of media and telecommunications companies, a proliferation of competitors, and convergence among various forms of media. &nbsp;As a result, our profitability could face increased pressure from consolidation of our customers, increased competition and new technologies.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Intellectual property </I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We rely on a combination of trademarks, trade names, copyrights, and other proprietary rights, as well as contractual arrangements, including licenses, to establish and protect our intellectual property and brand names. &nbsp;We believe our proprietary trademarks and other intellectual property rights are important to our continued success and our competitive position. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Dow Jones Indexes licenses, sometimes exclusively, our proprietary indexes and trademarks to exchanges and financial institutions for use as the basis of financial products. &nbsp;For example, Dow Jones has licensed the <I>Dow Jones Industrial Average</I> index and related trademarks for use as the basis of the DIAMONDS exchange-traded fund (ETF) and as the basis of exchange-traded options on the DIAMONDS ETF. &nbsp;Two lawsuits relevant to the index licensing industry are pending in federal court. &nbsp;Each of these suits is testing the scope of an index provider&#146;s ability to enforce its intellectual property rights with respect to certain licensing activities. In one action, Dow Jones sued the International Securities Exchange (ISE) and Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) concerning the unlicensed issuance and trading of exchange-traded options on the DIAMONDS ETF. &nbsp;The U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York issued a decision in that case in 2005 holding that neither ISE nor OCC requires a license from an index provider to issue or trade ETF options. &nbsp;Dow Jones&#146; appeal of this decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit was argued in February 2006; no decision has been issued. &nbsp;If the index provider&#146;s intellectual property rights are successfully challenged, our ability to license our index-related property for certain uses may be impaired and our revenues related to such licensing activities could be negatively impacted. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Acquisitions</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>From time to time, we seek out strategically and financially attractive acquisition opportunities. &nbsp;Such acquisitions will affect our costs, revenues, profitability and financial position. &nbsp;Acquisitions, including our recent acquisition of MarketWatch, involve risks and uncertainties, including difficulties in integrating acquired operations, diversions of management resources and loss of key employees, challenges with respect to operating new businesses, debt incurred in financing such acquisitions (including the related possible reduction in our credit ratings and increase in our cost of borrowing) and unanticipated problems and liabilities.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>New business opportunities and strategic alliances</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>There are substantial uncertainties associated with our efforts to leverage our brands to develop new business opportunities and to generate advertising and other revenues from these products. &nbsp;Initial timetables for the introduction and development of new products or services may not be achieved and price and profitability targets may not prove feasible. &nbsp;For example, we may be unable to successfully control expenses relating to our new Weekend Edition and may not achieve the gains from advertising revenues that we hope to achieve. &nbsp;We also face challenges in our attempts to achieve new strategic alliances and to improve the growth and profitability of existing strategic alliances. &nbsp;For example, we occasionally make non-controlling minority investments in public and private entities. &nbsp;We may have limited voting rights and, therefore, an inability to influence the direction of such entities. &nbsp;Therefore, the success of these ventures may be dependent upon the efforts of our partners, fellow investors and licensees. &nbsp;In addition, external factors, such as the development of competitive alternatives and market response, may negatively impact the success of these new opportunities and alliances.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR>
<BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>10</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>MDC/Cantor Fitzgerald legal proceeding</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We are currently party to a legal proceeding with Market Data Corp. (&#147;MDC&#148;) and Cantor Fitzgerald Securities with respect to our obligations, if any, under a guarantee issued to MDC and Cantor Fitzgerald Securities. &nbsp;The guarantee relates to certain annual &#147;minimum payments&#148; owed through October 2006 by Telerate under certain conditions for data acquired by Telerate from Cantor Fitzgerald Securities and MDC under contracts entered into by Telerate when Telerate was a subsidiary of ours. &nbsp;We have established a reserve ($264.7 million as of December 31, 2005) to cover payments we may need to make in connection with the guarantee to Cantor Fitzgerald Securities and MDC. However, if we are required to make payments under this guarantee, whether pursuant to a judgment in the litigation or a settlement agreement, those payments would negatively impact our cash flow. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Labor relations</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Approximately 32% of our domestic full-time employees are unionized. &nbsp;As a result, we are required to negotiate the wages, salaries, benefits, staffing levels and other terms with many of our employees collectively. &nbsp;Our results could be adversely affected if labor negotiations caused work interruptions or if we are unable to negotiate agreements on reasonable terms. &nbsp;In addition, our ability to make short-term adjustments to control fringe benefit costs is limited by the terms of our collective bargaining agreements in which benefits are fixed.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Newsprint prices</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Newsprint is our single most important raw material and represented approximately 8% of our total operating expenses in each of the last three years. &nbsp;The price of newsprint has historically been volatile. &nbsp;Consolidation in the North American newsprint industry has reduced the number of suppliers. &nbsp;This has led to paper mill closures and conversions to other grades of paper, which, in turn, have decreased overall newsprint capacity, resulted in price increases and increased the likelihood of more price increases in the future. &nbsp;Our operating results could be adversely affected if newsprint prices increase significantly.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>World events </I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:10pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Our results of operations are affected in various ways by events beyond our control, such as wars, political unrest, natural disasters and acts of terrorism which may occur in the future and could have a material adverse effect on our operating results.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Other facilities, owned in fee with a total of approximately 1,210,150 square feet, house news, sales, administrative, technology and operational staff.&nbsp; These facilities are located in South Brunswick, New Jersey and Chicopee Falls, Massachusetts.&nbsp; The Company has leased about 174,500 square feet of its office space in South Brunswick to other companies, mainly including our 50% owned Factiva joint venture.&nbsp; </P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>11</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Ottaway operates in 21 locations, including a 24,000 square foot administrative headquarters in Campbell Hall, New York. &nbsp;These facilities are located in Santa Cruz and Stockton, California; Danbury, Connecticut; Kennebunk and York, Maine; Hyannis, New Bedford and Nantucket, Massachusetts; Traverse City, Michigan; Stratham and Portsmouth, New Hampshire; Middletown, Oneonta, and Plattsburgh, New York; Medford and Ashland, Oregon; and Stroudsburg, Danville and Sunbury, Pennsylvania. &nbsp;Local printing facilities, which include office space in certain locations, total approximately 900,000 square feet. &nbsp;All of these facilities are owned in fee, with the exception of the Maine facilities, which are leased. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company believes that its current facilities are suitable and adequate, well maintained and in good condition. &nbsp;Older facilities have been modernized and expanded to meet present and anticipated needs.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<TABLE style="margin-right:48.25pt; font-size:10pt" cellspacing=0><TR><TD valign=top width=73.867><P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>ITEM 3. </B></P>
</TD><TD valign=top width=637.2><P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>LEGAL PROCEEDINGS. &nbsp;</B></P>
</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On November 13, 2001, the Company instituted a lawsuit in the Supreme Court of the State of New York against Market Data Corp. (MDC) and Cantor Fitzgerald Securities (together with its affiliates, Cantor) seeking a declaratory judgment with respect to the Company&#146;s obligations, if any, under a guarantee issued to MDC and Cantor. &nbsp;The guarantee relates to certain annual &#147;minimum payments&#148; owed by Telerate under certain conditions for data acquired by Telerate from Cantor Fitzgerald and MDC under contracts entered into when Telerate was a subsidiary of the Company, and is described in Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In this lawsuit the Company has asked the court to find that the Company does not and will not owe any payment under the contract guarantee through October 2006. &nbsp;In the alternative, the Company has asked the court to find that if any amount is owed, it must be reduced by amounts that Cantor and MDC receive or should have received from other distribution of the data after Telerate stopped receiving the government securities data from Cantor and MDC. &nbsp;MDC has asserted counterclaims demanding payment of $10.2 million (allegedly the balance owed by Telerate on November 15, 2001), interest, attorneys&#146; fees, specific performance of the guarantee, and a declaratory judgment as to the validity and interpretation of the guarantee through October 2006. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Cantor also commenced a separate lawsuit in the Supreme Court of the State of New York (since consolidated with the Company&#146;s case) seeking payment of $10 million (allegedly the balance of the November 2001 minimum payment), payment of $250 million in breach of contract damages, specific performance of the guarantee, a declaration that the guarantee remains in full force and effect, payment of approximately $16 million allegedly owed by Telerate and guaranteed by the Company in the guarantee for the distribution of certain other data, attorneys&#146; fees, interest, and other relief. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The trial court in January 2003 denied motions by each of the parties that their own claims for relief be granted and that competing claims be dismissed. &nbsp;Appeals from those decisions were not pursued, and discovery has concluded. &nbsp;On January 25, 2006, the trial court denied the bulk of the parties' motions for summary judgment, leaving the resolution of the case for trial. &nbsp;The Court did grant Dow Jones' motion for summary judgment on a small issue in the case. &nbsp;The Court did not set a trial date, but has directed the parties to appear before it at a settlement conference in early March 2006. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<TABLE style="margin-right:48.25pt; font-size:10pt" cellspacing=0><TR><TD valign=top width=73.867><P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>ITEM 4.</B></P>
</TD><TD valign=top width=637.2><P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>SUBMISSION OF MATTERS TO A VOTE OF SECURITY HOLDERS.</B></P>
</TD></TR>

<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Executive Officers of the Registrant&nbsp; </B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Each executive officer is elected annually to serve at the pleasure of the Board of Directors.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Peter R. Kann, age 63, Chairman of the Board since July 1991, served as Chief Executive Officer from January 1991 until February 2006. Mr. Kann served as Publisher of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> from January 1989 to July 2002, President from July 1989 to July 1991, Chief Operating Officer from July 1989 to December 1990, Executive Vice President from 1985 to 1989 and Associate Publisher of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> from 1979 to 1988.&nbsp; Mr. Kann, who is the spouse of Ms. House, joined the Company in 1964.&nbsp; </P>

Zannino, age 47, Chief Executive Officer since February 2006, served as Chief Operating Officer from July 2002 until February 2006, Executive Vice President from February 2001 to February 2006 and served as Chief Financial Officer from February 2001 until July 2002.&nbsp; Before joining Dow Jones, Mr. Zannino was Executive Vice President of Liz Claiborne, Inc., having joined in 1998 as Senior Vice President, Finance &amp; Administration and Chief Financial Officer.&nbsp; Previously, Mr. Zannino worked briefly as Chief Financial Officer of General Signal Corporation, prior to that company's sale, and before that for five years at Saks Holdings Inc., where he ultimately served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. </P>

Gordon Crovitz, age 47, Executive Vice President, President, Dow Jones Consumer Media Group, and Publisher of The Wall Street Journal Franchise since February 2006, served as Senior Vice President and President, Electronic Publishing and Senior Vice President/Electronic Publishing from October 1998 to February 2006, and as Vice President/Planning and Development from November 1997 to October 1998.&nbsp; Managing Director for Telerate's Asia/Pacific operation from September 1996 to November 1997.&nbsp; Editor and Publisher of Review Publishing Company from July 1993 to September 1996.&nbsp; Mr. Crovitz joined the Company in 1981.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:54pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:558pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:54pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:558pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:54pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:558pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In 1998 the Company&#146;s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of $800 million of the Company&#146;s common stock and in September 2000 authorized the repurchase of an additional $500 million of the Company&#146;s common stock. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005, approximately $326.4 million remained under board authorization for share repurchases. &nbsp;The Company has not repurchased any shares of its common stock since the first quarter of 2003.</P>
