<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center><B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center><B>DOW JONES &amp; COMPANY, INC.</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U>NOTE 1: &nbsp;SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>NATURE OF OPERATIONS</B> - Dow Jones &amp; Company (the Company) is a global provider of business and financial news and information through newspapers, newswires, newsletters, magazines, the Internet, indexes, television and radio. &nbsp;In addition, the Company owns certain general-interest community newspapers throughout the U.S. &nbsp;Advertising revenue is the Company&#146;s major revenue source.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B> include the accounts of the Company and its majority-owned subsidiaries. &nbsp;All significant intercompany transactions are eliminated in consolidation. &nbsp;The equity method of accounting is used for investments in other companies in which the Company has significant influence; generally this represents common stock ownership or partnership equity of at least 20% and not more than 50% (see Note 5).</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>RECLASSIFICATIONS</B> of certain amounts for prior years have been recorded to conform to the current year presentation.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>CASH EQUIVALENTS</B> are highly liquid investments with an original maturity of three months or less when purchased.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE</B> are reported net of an allowance for doubtful accounts, which is an estimate of amounts that may not be collectible. &nbsp;The Company extends credit to advertisers, subscribers and certain other customers based on an evaluation of the financial condition of the customer. &nbsp;Collateral is not generally required from customers. &nbsp;The allowance for doubtful accounts is based on historical trends, review of aging categories and the specific identification of certain customers that are at risk of not paying. &nbsp;Historically, actual write-offs of bad debt have been insignificant, less than 0.5% of revenues.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>NEWSPRINT INVENTORY</B> is stated at the lower of cost or market. &nbsp;The cost of newsprint is computed by the last-in, first-out (LIFO) method. &nbsp;If newsprint inventory had been valued by the average cost method, it would have been approximately $9.1 million and $7.7 million higher in 2005 and 2004, respectively.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>INVESTMENTS</B> in marketable equity securities, all of which are classified as available for sale, are carried at their market value in Other Investments on the consolidated balance sheets. &nbsp;The unrealized gains or losses from these investments are recorded directly to Stockholders&#146; Equity. &nbsp;Any decline in market value below the investment&#146;s original cost that is determined to be other-than-temporary as well as any realized gains or losses would be recognized in income (see Note 14).</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>PLANT, PROPERTY AND EQUIPMENT</B> are recorded at cost and depreciation is computed using straight-line or declining-balance methods over the estimated useful lives: 10 to 40 years for building and improvements, 3 to 25 years for machinery and equipment and 3 to 5 years for software. &nbsp;The 25-year life is applicable to the Company&#146;s press equipment. &nbsp;The cost of leasehold improvements is amortized over the lesser of the useful lives or the terms of the respective leases. &nbsp;Upon retirement or sale, the cost of disposed assets and the related accumulated depreciation are deducted from the respective accounts and the resulting gain or loss is included in income. &nbsp;The cost of construction of certain long-term assets includes capitalized interest, which is amortized over the life of the related assets. &nbsp;Interest capitalized in 2005, 2004 and 2003 was insignificant. &nbsp;Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred. &nbsp;Major renewals, betterments and additions are capitalized.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>GOODWILL AND OTHER INTANGIBLES</B> represent the excess purchase price of an acquisition over the fair value of other assets acquired, net of liabilities assumed, at the time the acquisition is made. &nbsp;An intangible with a finite life is amortized over its useful life, while an intangible with an indefinite life, including goodwill, is not amortized.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company tests goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible asset values at least annually for impairment. &nbsp;The balance of goodwill and other intangibles is assigned to a reporting unit, which is defined as an operating segment or one level below the operating segment. &nbsp;To determine whether an impairment exists, the carrying value of the reporting unit is compared with its fair value. &nbsp;An impairment loss would be recognized to the extent that the carrying value of the reporting unit exceeded its fair value. &nbsp;Fair value estimates are based on quoted market values in active markets, if available. &nbsp;If quoted market prices are not available, the estimate of fair value is based on various valuation techniques, including discounted value of estimated future cash flows, market multiples or appraised valuations.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Other intangible assets include acquired subscription accounts, which are amortized over 2 to 25 years, acquired advertising accounts are amortized over 3 to 12 years, developed technology intangibles are amortized over 4 to 6 years and other amortizable intangibles, including conference sponsorships, are amortized over 2 to 6 years. &nbsp;Other intangibles not subject to amortization consist principally of masthead and tradenames (see Note 3).</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>48</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>DEFERRED INCOME TAXES</B> are provided for temporary differences in bases between financial statement and income tax assets and liabilities. &nbsp;Deferred income taxes are recalculated annually at tax rates then in effect. &nbsp;The Company records a valuation allowance to reduce its deferred tax assets to the amount that is more likely than not to be realized. &nbsp;Currently, the Company maintains a tax valuation allowance on deferred tax assets related to its capital loss carryforward. &nbsp;While the Company has considered ongoing prudent and feasible tax planning strategies in assessing the need for the valuation allowance, in the event the Company were to determine that it would be able to realize all or a portion of its net deferred tax assets, an adjustment to the deferred tax asset would increase income in the period such determination was made. &nbsp;Likewise, should the Company subsequently determine that it would not be able to realize all or a portion of its net deferred tax assets in the future, an adjustment to the deferred tax asset would be charged to income in the period such determination was made. &nbsp;As part of the MarketWatch acquisition, the Company acquired a non-operating loss carryforward (see Note 10). </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>FOREIGN CURRENCY TRANSLATION</B> of assets and liabilities is determined at the appropriate year-end exchange rates, while results of operations are translated at the average rates of exchange in effect throughout the year. &nbsp;The resultant translation adjustments for subsidiaries whose functional currency is not the U.S. dollar are recorded directly to comprehensive income in Stockholders&#146; Equity. &nbsp;Gains or losses arising from remeasurement of financial statements for foreign subsidiaries where the U.S. dollar is the functional currency as well as from all foreign currency transactions are included in income. &nbsp;Foreign exchange included in Other, net in the income statement totaled a gain of $2 million in 2005, a loss of $1.3 million in 2004 and a gain of $0.1 million in 2003. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>FOREIGN CURRENCY-EXCHANGE CONTRACTS</B> are designated as cash flow hedges of anticipated operating expenses that are denominated in foreign currencies. &nbsp;Revenues of the Company are largely collected in U.S. dollars. &nbsp;These contracts are entered into to mitigate foreign exchange volatility relative to the currencies hedged. &nbsp;Realized gains or losses on foreign currency forward contracts are recognized currently through income and generally offset the transaction gains or losses on the foreign currency cash flows which they are intended to hedge. &nbsp;Unrealized gains or losses, arising from changes in fair value, are recorded as a component of comprehensive income. &nbsp;The Company also enters into foreign currency forward exchange contracts to limit the cash flow and earnings volatility that results from remeasuring certain foreign currency payables at prevailing exchange rates. &nbsp;The unrealized gains or losses of these forward contracts are recognized in Other, net in the income statement. &nbsp;Hedge effectiveness for these foreign currency-exchange contracts is assessed, at least quarterly, by measuring the correlation of the contract to the expected future cash flows (see Note 14).</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>REVENUE</B> from advertising, which is net of commissions, is recognized in the period in which the advertisement is displayed. &nbsp;The Company's advertising rate card reflects certain volume-based discounts and certain customers also qualify for volume-based bonus advertisements. &nbsp;These programs require management to make certain estimates regarding future advertising volume. &nbsp;The estimated rebates and bonus advertisements are recorded as reductions of revenue in the periods the advertisements are displayed and are revised as necessary based on actual volume realized. &nbsp;For the years ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, the Company&#146;s estimated rebate and bonus advertising reserves totaled $15.5 million, $8.5 million and $12.4 million, respectively and were classified as a liability. &nbsp;Certain online-related advertising revenues are based on the number of &quot;impressions&#148; delivered and are recognized as impressions occur, while other online advertising revenues are based on a fixed duration campaign and are recognized ratably over the term of the campaign.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Revenue recognition from subscriptions to the Company's print publications and information services is recognized in income as earned, pro rata on a per-issue basis, over the subscription period. &nbsp;Circulation revenue includes sales to retail outlets/newsstands, which are subject to returns. &nbsp;The Company records these retail sales upon delivery, net of estimated returns. &nbsp;These estimated returns are based on historical return rates and are revised as necessary based on actual returns experienced. &nbsp;The Company&#146;s estimated returns reserves totaled approximately $3 million for each of the years ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003. &nbsp;Costs in connection with the procurement of subscriptions are charged to expense as incurred. &nbsp;Revenue from licensing the Dow Jones Averages includes both upfront one-time fees and ongoing revenue. &nbsp;Both upfront fees and ongoing licensing revenue are recognized in income as earned over the license period.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>ADVERTISING COSTS</B>, which include circulation marketing as well as trade advertising, are expensed as incurred. &nbsp;Advertising costs included in selling, administrative and general expenses were $108 million in 2005, $83.1 million in 2004 and $73.3 million in 2003.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>PENSION AND OTHER POSTRETIREMENT PLANS</B> are provided by the Company to a majority of its employees through defined contribution plans based on compensation levels. &nbsp;The Company matches employee contributions up to a determined percentage. &nbsp;The defined contribution plans are funded currently. &nbsp;Some of the Company&#146;s subsidiaries provide defined benefit plans based on length of service and compensation. &nbsp;The Company also sponsors a defined benefit postretirement medical plan to certain retirees who meet specific length of service and age requirements. &nbsp;It is the Company&#146;s policy to fund postretirement benefits as medical claims are incurred. &nbsp;The estimated cost for both the defined pension benefit and the postretirement medical plans, which is actuarially derived, is recorded over the employee&#146;s expected service period (see Note 9). &nbsp;The measurement date used for the majority of plan assets and defined benefit obligations is December 31.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>49</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION </B>is accounted for in accordance with Accounting Principles Board Opinion No. 25 (APB 25), <I>&#147;Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees,&#148;</I> and its related interpretations. &nbsp;Under APB 25, pretax stock-based compensation charged to income, principally in relation to the Company&#146;s contingent stock rights, restricted stock units and restricted stock awards, was $10 million in 2005, $8.7 million in 2004 and $7.4 million in 2003 (see Note 12).</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In December 2004, the FASB issued Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 123 (revised 2004), &quot;<I>Share-Based Payment</I>&quot; (SFAS 123R). &nbsp;This statement eliminated the alternative to apply the intrinsic value measurement provisions of APB 25, to stock compensation awards issued to employees. &nbsp;Rather, SFAS 123R requires companies to measure the cost of employee services received in exchange for an award of equity instruments based on the grant-date fair value of the award. &nbsp;That cost will be recognized in the consolidated statement of income over the period during which an employee is required to provide services in exchange for the award, usually the vesting period. &nbsp;The Company will adopt SFAS 123R and the related FASB Staff Positions using the modified prospective application, one of several alternative transition methods, when it is effective for the Company on January 1, 2006. &nbsp;Management estimates that the adoption of SFAS 123R will result in additional expense of approximately $.04 per diluted share during 2006.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the fourth quarter of 2004, the Company, with approval from its Board of Directors, announced the acceleration of 2.2 million stock options, representing all unvested options granted and outstanding starting after 2002. &nbsp;The Company&#146;s decision to accelerate the vesting of certain outstanding stock option grants was made as part of a broad review of long-term incentive compensation in light of changes in market practices and accounting changes. &nbsp;Other changes to be implemented beyond accelerating the vesting of certain options include reducing overall equity grant levels, a change in the mix of grants, and applying a three-year &#147;cliff&#148; vesting schedule to future grants of stock options. &nbsp;Had the Company&#146;s stock-based compensation been determined by the fair-value based method of SFAS 123, the Company&#146;s net income and earnings per share would have been as follows:</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U>NOTE 2: &nbsp;ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSITIONS</U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><U><BR></U></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2005</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Acquisition of MarketWatch</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On January 21, 2005, the Company completed its acquisition of MarketWatch, Inc. (MarketWatch) for a purchase price of approximately $532 million. &nbsp;The purchase price consisted of net cash tendered totaling approximately $502 million to acquire the 28.2 million outstanding common shares of MarketWatch; the exchange of 1.2 million stock options valued at $25 million using the Black-Scholes option pricing model; and, direct third party transaction costs of approximately $5 million. &nbsp;This acquisition was financed by $439 million of short-term commercial paper borrowings and cash, including cash received from MarketWatch of $74 million. &nbsp;In February 2005, the Company refinanced $225 million of its commercial paper borrowings with three-year bonds bearing a fixed interest rate of 3.875%. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>MarketWatch is a provider of business news, financial information and analytical tools and operates two Web sites: MarketWatch.com and BigCharts.com. These free, advertising-supported sites serve visitors with market news and information. &nbsp;MarketWatch also operates the MarketWatch Information Services group, which is a licensor of market news, data, investment analysis tools and other online applications to financial services firms, media companies and corporations. &nbsp;The Company has fully integrated MarketWatch into the Consumer Electronic Publishing business, with integration of its news, advertising sales, information technology and back office operations. &nbsp;The MarketWatch acquisition complements The Wall Street Journal Online network and expands the Company&#146;s online audience and advertising revenues. &nbsp;These factors contributed to a purchase price in excess of the fair market value of the net tangible and intangible assets acquired from MarketWatch, and as a result, the Company recorded goodwill in connection with this transaction.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>51</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company has allocated $28.2 million to amortizable intangible assets consisting of customer-related intangible assets and developed technology with weighted-average useful lives of six and four years, respectively. &nbsp;The pattern of economic benefits to be derived from certain intangible assets is estimated to be greater in the initial period of ownership; accordingly, the Company has recorded accelerated amortization expense for certain intangible assets. &nbsp;Further, $29 million has been allocated to trade names and $391.2 million to goodwill, which will not be amortized. &nbsp;Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price over the fair value of the net tangible and intangible assets acquired, and is not deductible for tax purposes. &nbsp;Liabilities assumed include approximately $7.9 million of restructuring costs related to severance of approximately 50 MarketWatch employees and other contractual commitments.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Exchange of Cross Shareholdings</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>During the second quarter of 2005, the Company and the von Holtzbrinck Group completed its exchange of cross shareholdings. &nbsp;In exchange for the Company&#146;s 10% interest in <I>Handelsblatt</I>, the Company received the remaining 10% minority interest in <I>The Wall Street Journal Europe</I> that it did not already own; an 11.5% increase in its interest in a Czech Republic business periodical, effectively increasing the Company&#146;s interest to 23%; and, $6 million in cash. &nbsp;The transaction was accounted for at fair value and the Company recorded a gain of $13.2 million ($8.3 million, net of taxes) in connection with the disposal of its interest in <I>Handelsblatt</I>.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The step acquisition of the remaining 10% interest in <I>The Wall Street Journal Europe</I> resulted in a purchase price allocation to goodwill of $4.4 million and other intangibles of $1.7 million. &nbsp;The other intangibles consisted of advertising accounts valued at $0.7 million and subscription accounts valued at $0.1 million. &nbsp;These intangibles will be amortized on a straight-line basis over 8 years. &nbsp;The remaining $0.9 million represented acquired masthead which has an indefinite life.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Disposition of F.F. Soucy</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In April 2005, the Company concluded the sale of its 39.9% minority interest in F.F. Soucy Inc., a Canadian newsprint mill, to its majority owner, Brant-Allen Industries, Inc. &nbsp;The sale price of $40 million resulted in a gain of $9.6 million ($9.4 million, net of taxes) in the second quarter. &nbsp;As part of the sale the Company provided Brant-Allen a limited indemnification for certain income tax matters. &nbsp;The Company estimated its obligation under this indemnification to be $2.2 million and recorded this amount as a liability and a reduction to the gain on sale.&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><U><BR></U></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2004</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Acquisition of remaining interest in OsterDow Jones</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On July 7, 2004, the Company acquired the remaining two-thirds interest in OsterDow Jones Commodity News for $1.6 million. &nbsp;The new operation, &#147;Dow Jones Commodities Service,&#148; was combined with the Company&#146;s Dow Jones Newswires business. &nbsp;The step acquisition resulted in a purchase price allocation to goodwill of $1.4 million and tangible assets of $0.2 million.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>52</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Acquisition of remaining interest in VWD news operations and disposition of non-news assets of VWD &nbsp;</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On April 2, 2004, the Company acquired the remaining interest in the news operations of Vereinigte Wirtschaftsdienste GmbH (VWD), a German newswires business, for $12.1 million. &nbsp;The acquired business consists of financial newswires and business newsletters, which have been combined into the Company&#146;s Dow Jones Newswires business, under the brand name Dow Jones-VWD News. &nbsp;Dow Jones was a minority shareholder in VWD. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The acquisition was accounted for at fair value as a step acquisition in accordance with SFAS 141, &#147;<I>Business Combinations</I>.&#148; The acquisition resulted in a purchase price allocation to goodwill of $9.3 million, other intangibles of $1.7 million and net assets of $0.5 million. &nbsp;The other intangibles consist primarily of subscription contracts that will be amortized over their estimated useful life of 8 years. &nbsp;Substantially all of the acquired goodwill and intangible assets will be deductible for tax purposes. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On April 2, 2004, simultaneous with the Company&#146;s acquisition of the remaining interest in the news operations of VWD, VWD sold its non-news assets to a third party, resulting in cash proceeds to Dow Jones of $6.7 million. &nbsp;As a result of this sale, the Company recorded an after-tax gain of $1.8 million in the second quarter of 2004. &nbsp;Following the transaction, the Company had no involvement in the continuing operations of the disposed business. &nbsp;The consideration was received at the time of the sale and a gain was recognized pursuant to the guidance in Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic 5E. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Acquisition of Alternative Investor</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On March 19, 2004, the Company completed its acquisition of Alternative Investor from Wicks Business Information for $85 million plus net working capital. &nbsp;The $85 million purchase price could be increased by $5 million, payable in 2008, based on the performance of the acquired business. &nbsp;The acquisition was primarily funded by the issuance of debt under the Company&#146;s commercial paper program. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Alternative Investor is a provider of newsletters, databases and industry conferences for the venture-capital and private-equity markets, and has been combined into the Company&#146;s Dow Jones Newswires business. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The acquisition resulted in a purchase price allocation to goodwill of $78.1 million, other intangibles of $18.6 million and net liabilities of $11.4 million (principally acquired unearned revenue). &nbsp;Substantially all of the acquired goodwill and intangible assets will be deductible for tax purposes. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2003 </I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Non-monetary Exchange of Equity Holdings </I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In December 2003, the Company and the von Holtzbrinck Group exchanged equity shareholdings so as to increase the Company&#146;s ownership of <I>The Wall Street Journal Europe </I>to 90% from 51% and reduce the Company&#146;s ownership of the von Holtzbrinck Group&#146;s business daily, <I>Handelsblatt</I>, to 10% from 22%, with news and advertising relationships continuing. &nbsp;The transaction was accounted for at fair value in accordance with EITF 01-2 <I>&#147;Interpretations of APB 29&#148;</I>, as a disposition of 12% of <I>Handelsblatt </I>in exchange for the acquisition of an additional 39% interest in <I>The Wall Street Journal Europe. &nbsp;</I>The Company recorded a gain of $18.7 million ($11.4 million after taxes), on the disposal of the 12% interest in <I>Handelsblatt</I>, as the risks of ownership were relinquished at the time of sale. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The purchase of 39% of <I>The Wall Street Journal Europe </I>resulted in the acquisition of goodwill of $16.9 million and other intangibles of $6.5 million. &nbsp;The other intangibles consisted of advertising accounts valued at $2.5 million and subscription accounts valued at $0.2 million. &nbsp;These intangibles will be amortized on a straight-line basis over 8 years. &nbsp;The remaining $3.8 million represented acquired masthead which has an indefinite life. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Acquisition of Technologic Partners </I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On September 2, 2003, the Company purchased Technologic Partners, a closely-held publications and events firm for $2.7 million. &nbsp;Technologic Partners, which has eight online newsletters and produces six conference events annually, was combined with the Newsletters group within Dow Jones Newswires. &nbsp;The purchase resulted in the acquisition of goodwill of $3.4 million and other intangibles of $0.5 million, to be amortized on a straight-line basis over five years. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Based on the performance of the acquired business, and pursuant to the purchase agreement, in October 2004, the Company made an additional payment of $3.4 million for Technologic Partners. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Acquisition of The Record of Stockton, California </I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On May 5, 2003, the Company&#146;s Ottaway Newspaper subsidiary acquired <I>The Record of Stockton, California </I>from Omaha World-Herald Company for $146 million ($144 million in cash, plus net working capital). </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The purchase resulted in the acquisition of tangible net assets of $12 million, goodwill of $76.6 million and other intangibles of $58.2 million. &nbsp;The acquired goodwill and intangible assets will be deductible for tax purposes. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Had the 2003 acquisitions been completed as of January 1, 2003 the impact on the Company&#146;s revenues, net income and earnings per share would not have been material. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Resolution of Telerate Sale Loss Contingencies </I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the first quarter of 2003, the Company recorded a gain of $59.8 million on the resolution of certain loss contingencies resulting from the sale of its former Telerate subsidiary to Bridge. &nbsp;The reserve for loss contingencies was established as part of the loss on the sale of Telerate in 1998 and related to various claims that arose out of the Stock Purchase Agreement, including a purchase price adjustment related to working capital, an indemnification undertaking and other actual and potential claims and counter-claims between the Company and Bridge. &nbsp;In February 2001, Bridge declared bankruptcy. In March 2003, these matters were resolved by the bankruptcy court, and the Company&#146;s contingent liabilities were thereby extinguished.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U><BR></U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U>NOTE 3: &nbsp;GOODWILL AND OTHER INTANGIBLE ASSETS </U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>As of January 1, 2002, the Company adopted the provisions of SFAS 142, &#147;<I>Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets.&quot;</I> &nbsp;SFAS 142 requires that an intangible asset that is acquired either individually or with a group of other assets be initially recognized and measured based on fair value. &nbsp;An intangible with a finite life is amortized over its useful life, while an intangible with an indefinite life, including goodwill, is not amortized. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The workforce reductions related to the restructuring actions are substantially complete. &nbsp;The remaining reserve relates primarily to continuing payments for employees that have already been terminated and is expected to be paid over the next twelve months.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><U><BR></U></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2005</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the second quarter of 2005, the Company recorded a restructuring charge of $11.4 million ($6.9 million, net of taxes) primarily reflecting employee severance related to a workforce reduction of about 120 full-time employees. &nbsp;Most of the charge related to the Company&#146;s efforts to reposition its international print and online operations but also included headcount reductions at other parts of the business. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>56</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2004</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the fourth quarter of 2004, the Company recorded a restructuring charge of $6.7 million ($4.0 million, net of taxes) primarily reflecting employee severance related to a workforce reduction of about 100 employees. &nbsp;The majority of this charge was related to employee severance in connection with the Company&#146;s decision to publish <I>Far Eastern Economic Review</I> (FEER) as a monthly periodical beginning in December 2004, with the balance of the charge related to headcount reductions in circulation and international operations. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On September 11, 2001, the Company&#146;s headquarters at the World Financial Center (WFC) sustained damage from debris and dust as a result of the terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center. &nbsp;Approximately 60% of the floor space, including furniture and related equipment, had been deemed a total loss. &nbsp;In the fourth quarter 2001, the Company recorded a charge of $32.2 million as a result of its decision to permanently re-deploy certain personnel and to abandon four of seven floors that were leased at its WFC headquarters. &nbsp;This charge primarily reflected the Company&#146;s rent obligation through May 2005 on this vacated space. &nbsp;In the first quarter of 2004, the Company decided to extend the term of its lease for one of the floors that was previously abandoned and reoccupy this floor with personnel from another of its New York locations, whose lease term was expiring. &nbsp;As a result, the Company reversed $2.8 million ($1.7 million, net of taxes) of the remaining lease obligation reserve for the previously abandoned floor at WFC.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2003</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company has insurance policies that cover property damage, extra expenses and business interruption related to the September 11 disaster. &nbsp;In the second quarter of 2003, the Company recorded a gain of $18.4 million ($11.1 million, net of taxes) reflecting the settlement of its business interruption insurance claim for loss of operating income suffered as a result of the terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U><BR></U></B></P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Write-Down of Equity Investments</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In December 2005, the Company completed the disposal of its 50% interests in both CNBC Europe and CNBC Asia (collectively CNBC International), as well as its 25% interest in CNBC World, to NBC Universal for nominal consideration pursuant to a July 2005 agreement. &nbsp;Through 2006 the Company will continue to provide access to news resources and other services to CNBC International, nonexclusively. &nbsp;There are no plans to alter the licensing relationship in the U.S. between the Company and CNBC.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the second quarter of 2005, in connection with the binding agreement reached with NBC Universal, the Company determined that an other-than-temporary decline in the value of its investments in CNBC International and CNBC World had occurred and, as a result, the Company recorded a charge of $35.9 million ($36.7 million, including taxes), largely reflecting the write-down of the investments&#146; carrying value ($32 million), with the remainder primarily reflecting the additional firmly committed cash payment for which there was no future economic benefit to the Company.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The revolving credit agreements contain restrictive covenants, including a limitation on the ratio of consolidated indebtedness to consolidated cash flow and a requirement to maintain a minimum ratio of consolidated cash flow to consolidated interest expense. &nbsp;On August 29, 2005, the Company amended its 5-year credit agreement dated June 25, 2001 and its 5-year credit agreement dated June 21, 2004 to temporarily increase the leverage covenant, from 3.5x to 4.0x, for each of the two quarters ended September 30, 2005 and December 31, 2005. &nbsp;At December 31, 2005, the Company was in compliance with respect to both of these restrictive covenants then in effect, with the leverage ratio equaling less than 3.0x. &nbsp;The Company&#146;s original restrictive covenants will be effective for periods subsequent to December 31, 2005. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>58</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Borrowings may be made either in Eurodollars with interest that approximates the applicable Eurodollar rate or in U.S. dollars with interest that approximates the bank's prime rate, its certificate of deposit rate or the federal funds rate. &nbsp;A quarterly fee is payable on the commitment which the Company may terminate or reduce at any time. &nbsp;The quarterly fee, which is dependent on the Company&#146;s debt rating issued by S&amp;P and Moody's, ranges from .08% to .10%. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005 and 2004, no amounts were borrowed under the revolving credit lines. &nbsp;The Company intends to extend the revolving credit agreements prior to their expiration.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Interest payments were $16.3 million in 2005, $3.8 million in 2004 and $2.7 million in 2003.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U>NOTE 7: &nbsp;CONTRACT GUARANTEE </U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In 1998, the Company completed the sale of its former subsidiary, Telerate, to Bridge Information Systems, Inc. (Bridge). &nbsp;Under the terms of the sale, the Company retained its guarantee of payments under certain circumstances of certain annual minimum payments for data acquired by Telerate from Cantor Fitzgerald Securities (Cantor) and Market Data Corporation (MDC) under contracts entered into during the period when Telerate was a subsidiary of the Company (contract guarantee). &nbsp;The annual minimum payments average approximately $50 million per year through October 2006 under certain conditions. &nbsp;Bridge agreed to indemnify the Company for any liability the Company incurred under the contract guarantee with respect to periods subsequent to Bridge's purchase of Telerate. &nbsp;However, Bridge filed for bankruptcy protection on February 15, 2001, after unsuccessful attempts to reorganize its operations and arrange for additional financing. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company believes that Cantor and MDC have the obligation to cover, mitigate or otherwise reduce and/or avoid any losses or damages under these circumstances, including by securing the best possible commercial terms for the supply of the subject data to a third party or parties. &nbsp;Cantor and MDC deny that they have this obligation. &nbsp;The Company believes that any and all amounts which are received by Cantor and/or MDC in respect of such data would reduce any liability that the Company might have under the contract guarantee. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2000, there was a high degree of uncertainty, however, as to what value the data might have in the marketplace; whether an agreement would be reached by Cantor and/or MDC to supply the data to a third party or parties, the financial position of such party or parties; the timing of any such agreement, and various related factors. &nbsp;Therefore, it was not possible for the Company to determine with any certainty that any such offsets would in fact be realized, or at what time or in what amounts. &nbsp;Consequently, in December 2000, the Company established a reserve in the amount of $255 million representing the present value of the total estimated annual minimum payments of about $300 million over the remainder of the contract (through October 2006 and using a discount rate of approximately 6%). &nbsp;In 2001, a portion of this obligation was subsequently paid by Bridge during its bankruptcy proceedings and the Company adjusted its reserve accordingly.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Earnings in 2005, 2004 and 2003 included accretion charges of $4.1 million, $6.9 million and $9.5 million, respectively, which increased the reserve balance as of December 31, 2005 to $264.7 million, all of which is classified as current based on the original due dates of the contract.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On November 13, 2001, the Company instituted a lawsuit in the Supreme Court of the State of New York against MDC and Cantor seeking a declaratory judgment with respect to the Company&#146;s obligations, if any, under the guarantee. &nbsp;In this lawsuit the Company has asked the court to find that the Company does not and will not owe any payment under the contract guarantee through October 2006. &nbsp;In the alternative, the Company has asked the court to find that if any amount is owed, it must be reduced by amounts that Cantor and MDC receive or should have received from other distribution of the data. &nbsp;MDC has asserted counterclaims demanding payment of $10.2 million (allegedly the balance owed by Telerate on November 15, 2001), interest, attorneys&#146; fees, specific performance of the guarantee, and a declaratory judgment as to the validity and interpretation of the guarantee through October 2006. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Cantor also commenced a separate lawsuit in the Supreme Court of the State of New York (since consolidated with the Company&#146;s case) seeking payment of $10 million (allegedly the balance of the November 2001 minimum payment), payment of $250 million in breach of contract damages, specific performance of the guarantee, a declaration that the guarantee remains in full force and effect, payment of approximately $16 million allegedly owed by Telerate and guaranteed by the Company in the guarantee for the distribution of certain other data, attorneys' fees, interest and other relief. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The trial court in January 2003 denied motions by each of the parties that their own claims for relief be granted and that competing claims be dismissed. &nbsp;Appeals from those decisions were not pursued, and discovery has concluded. &nbsp;On January 25, 2006, the trial court denied the bulk of the parties' motions for summary judgment, leaving the resolution of the case for trial. &nbsp;The Court did grant Dow Jones' motion for summary judgment on a small issue in the case. &nbsp;The Court did not set a trial date, but has directed the parties to appear before it at a settlement conference in early March 2006. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>59</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Due to the stage of the lawsuit at December 31, 2005, it is not possible to determine whether the court will find that any obligation the Company had under the guarantee may be dismissed or reduced. &nbsp;Accordingly, the Company believes the balance of the reserve continues to be appropriate. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>While it is not possible to predict with certainty the ultimate outcome of this litigation, the Company believes the likelihood of a loss exceeding the amount reserved is remote; however, it is possible that such loss could be less than the amount reserved. </P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Other Guarantees and Contingencies</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In addition to the litigation that is separately disclosed in Note 7 of this Form 10-K, there are various libel actions, legal proceedings and other matters that have arisen in the ordinary course of business that represent possible contingencies of the Company and its subsidiaries. &nbsp;In the opinion of management, based on advice of legal counsel, the ultimate outcome to the Company and its subsidiaries as a result of these legal proceedings and other matters will not have a material effect on the Company&#146;s financial statements. &nbsp;In addition, the Company has insurance coverage for many of these matters.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company&#146;s bylaws provide for indemnification of officers and directors prosecuted in a criminal action or sued in a civil action or proceeding to the full extent permitted by the Delaware General Corporation Law. &nbsp;The maximum potential amount of future payments the Company could be required to make under these indemnification provisions is unlimited; however, the Company maintains directors' and officers' liability and corporation reimbursement insurance for the benefit of the Company and its directors and officers. &nbsp;The policy provides coverage for certain amounts paid as indemnification pursuant to the provisions of Delaware law and the Company&#146;s bylaws. &nbsp;As a result of its insurance coverage, the Company believes that the estimated fair value of these indemnification provisions is minimal.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company enters into indemnification agreements in its ordinary course of business, typically with companies from which it is acquiring or to which it is selling businesses, partners in joint ventures, licensees and licensors, and service providers and contractors. &nbsp;Under these agreements the Company generally indemnifies, holds harmless, and agrees to reimburse the indemnified party for losses suffered or incurred by the indemnified party, as a result of the Company&#146;s activities or its breach of the agreement in question or in connection with any intellectual property infringement claim by any third party with respect to the Company's products. &nbsp;These indemnification obligations generally survive termination of the underlying agreement, either for some set number of years or perpetually. &nbsp;In some cases, the maximum potential amount of future payments the Company could be required to make under these indemnification obligations is unlimited. &nbsp;Other than the $2.2 million Brant-Allen Industries indemnification discussed in Note 2, the Company believes that the estimated fair value of these indemnity obligations is minimal. &nbsp;The Company has not incurred material costs to defend lawsuits or settle claims related to these indemnification provisions. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Newsprint is the Company&#146;s single most important raw material and represented approximately 8% of the Company&#146;s total operating expenses in each of the last three years. The Company has signed long-term contracts with certain newsprint suppliers for a substantial portion of its annual newsprint requirements and has discretion as to the timing of such purchases.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company has guaranteed payment for office space occupied by certain of its joint ventures. &nbsp;Partners of the Company in these joint ventures have either directly guaranteed their share of any payments required under these guarantees or agreed to indemnify the Company for 50% of any payments the Company may be required to make under these guarantees. &nbsp;The Company&#146;s share of this obligation totals $1.1 million through 2010.</P>

<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U>NOTE 9: &nbsp;PENSION AND OTHER POSTRETIREMENT PLANS</U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Employee Pensions</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company provides retirement plans for a majority of its employees who meet specific length of service requirements through several plans.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company&#146;s defined contribution plans cover a majority of its employees. &nbsp;The 401(k) Savings Plans are based on a fixed percentage of compensation and allow an employer matching opportunity up to a specified percentage. &nbsp;The contribution for each employee is limited to the amount deductible for income tax purposes. &nbsp;The annual cost of the plan is funded currently. &nbsp;The total costs related to defined contribution plans amounted to $45 million in 2005, $44.3 million in 2004 and $43.6 million in 2003.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Substantially all employees who are not covered by the defined contribution plans are covered by defined benefit pension plans. &nbsp;The Company&#146;s defined benefit pension plan benefits are based on years of service and compensation. &nbsp;The total cost of these defined benefit plans was $5.8 million in 2005, $2.8 million in 2004 and $8.0 million in 2003.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Postretirement Benefits other than Pensions</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>For a majority of its full-time employees, the Company sponsors defined benefit postretirement medical plans which provide lifetime health care benefits to retirees who meet specified length of service and age requirements, and their eligible dependents. &nbsp;The plans are unfunded.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act of 2003</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In December 2003, new Medicare prescription drug legislation was enacted into law. &nbsp;Beginning in 2006, this law adds a new prescription drug benefit under Medicare and also provides a federal subsidy to companies that sponsor retiree health care plans that provide a benefit that is at least &#147;actuarially equivalent&#148; to the Medicare plan. &nbsp;The subsidy amount, which is tax-free, is 28% of each Medicare eligible retiree&#146;s drug costs between $250 and $5,000.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the second quarter of 2004, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued FASB Staff Position (FSP) No. FAS 106-2, &#147;<I>Accounting and Disclosure Requirements Related to the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act of 2003.</I>&#148; The FSP clarified that companies eligible for federal subsidies under the Act should recognize the expected benefit as part of its measurement of its accumulated postretirement obligation. &nbsp;Accordingly in the second quarter 2004, the Company remeasured its postretirement obligation as of January 1, 2004 factoring in this expected benefit from Medicare. &nbsp;The remeasurement resulted in a reduction of the Company&#146;s accumulated postretirement benefit obligation by $24 million and reduced its expected annual 2004 postretirement expense by $3.6 million (a reduction of service cost by $1.2 million, interest cost by $1.5 million and recognized actuarial loss by $0.9 million).</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Plan amendment</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the fourth quarter of 2005, the Company announced modifications to the coverage under the Company&#146;s prescription drug plan which affects certain current employees who retire on or after April 1, 2006, and who do not meet certain other criteria that would exempt them from the modifications. &nbsp;These modifications require the substitution of the Medicare Part D prescription drug program (or a plan that matches the provisions of the Medicare Part D prescription drug program) beginning in 2007 in place of the Company&#146;s current drug plan. &nbsp;In addition, certain new employees hired after January 1, 2006 will not be eligible for any retiree health care benefits from the Company. &nbsp;Instead, those employees will be eligible for Medicare benefits. &nbsp;These modifications, which are expected to yield long-term savings for the Company, apply only to benefits that come into effect after retirement.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Basis for determining the discount rate</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company&#146;s discount rate was determined by projecting the plans&#146; expected future benefit payments, as defined for the projected benefit obligations, and discounting those expected payments using an average of yield curves constructed based on a large population of high-quality corporate bonds. &nbsp;The resulting discount rate reflects the matching of plan liability cash flows to the yield curves.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Basis for determining the expected asset return</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The expected long-term rate of return on assets assumption for the defined benefit plan was based on gross expected rates of return less anticipated expenses. &nbsp;The gross expected rates of return are the sum of expected real rates of return plus anticipated inflation. &nbsp;Real rates of return were derived for each asset class based on historical rates of returns. &nbsp;The anticipated inflation rate was then added to these expected real returns to arrive at the expected long-term rate of return on asset assumption. &nbsp;The expected long-term rate is then compared to actual historic investment performance of the plan assets and evaluated through consultation with investment advisors.&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Health care cost trend rate</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>A 9% annual rate of increase in the per capita costs of covered health care benefits was assumed for 2006, gradually decreasing to 5% by the year 2012 and remaining at that rate thereafter. &nbsp;The Company&#146;s health care cost trend rate assumed for 2005 was 10% decreasing to 5% by the year 2012.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Defined Benefit Pension Plan Assets</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The defined benefit pension plan&#146;s investment objective is to maximize long-term total return through a combination of income and capital appreciation with a prudent investment practice and assumption of a moderate risk level. &nbsp;The Company provides guidance to the investment manager who has responsibility for asset allocation within the following ranges: equity investments between 25% to 75%, debt securities between 25% to 75%, and cash equivalents from 0% to 50%. &nbsp;In addition, the investment manager may not allocate more than 35% to a specific industry or more than 5% to an individual company.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2005</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the fourth quarter 2005, the Company received a federal tax refund, including interest, related to the settlement of claims from previously filed returns. &nbsp;Pursuant to the settlement of these claims, during the fourth quarter of 2005, the Company recorded an adjustment of $8 million to its tax accounts and recorded interest income of $1.4 million ($0.9 million, net of taxes). &nbsp;The total impact of these items was an increase in net income of $8.9 million. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Income tax expense in the third quarter 2005 included a tax benefit of $1.1 million as a result of a favorable resolution of certain state and federal tax matters.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2004</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Income tax expense in 2004 included tax benefits of $5.7 million in the fourth quarter and $1.5 million in the third quarter as a result of the favorable resolution of certain federal tax matters. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I><BR>
<BR></I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>65</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>2003</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>In the third quarter of 2003, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) completed its audit of the Company&#146;s tax returns for the 1995 through 1998 tax periods, which had been amended for additional tax refunds. &nbsp;In October 2003, the Company received notification that the Congressional Joint Committee on Taxation had approved these claims for tax refunds of approximately $24 million. &nbsp;The Company received these refunds plus interest of approximately $6.7 million in the fourth quarter of 2003. &nbsp;Pursuant to the settlement of these claims, in the third quarter of 2003, the Company recorded an adjustment of $25 million to its tax reserve balance as a result of the resolution of certain tax matters and recorded interest income of $6.7 million ($4.0 million, net of taxes). &nbsp;The Company also recorded a provision of $9.5 million in the third quarter for loss contingencies relating to recent developments in certain other tax matters. &nbsp;The net effect of these items was an increase in net income of $19.5 million. &nbsp;</P>
