<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Capital Loss Carryforward</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>As of December 31, 2005, the Company had a capital loss carryforward remaining of about $454 million (a deferred tax asset of about $170 million, with a full valuation allowance). &nbsp;Approximately $164 million of this loss carryforward is recognized for tax purposes, the bulk of which expires in 2006. &nbsp;The remaining $290 million of capital loss carryforward, which primarily relates to the contract guarantee obligation (see Note 7), will be recognized for tax purposes only to the extent, if any, that the Company is required to make payment. &nbsp;If the Company is required to make any such payment, the resulting loss carryforward will be available for use five years from the year it is recognized.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company could not conclude that it was more likely than not that it would realize any net tax savings from capital loss carryforward prior to their expiration and believes the full valuation allowance reserve was appropriate at December 31, 2005.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Net Operating Loss Carryforward- acquired</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>As part of the MarketWatch acquisition, the Company acquired a net operating loss carryforward of approximately $110.7 million (a deferred tax asset of about $42.8 million). &nbsp;Approximately $16.8 million of this loss carryforward (or $6.2 million of tax benefit) was utilized in 2005. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005, the remaining loss carryforward, which is subject to annual limitations of its use, was $93.9 million (a deferred tax asset of about $36.6 million).</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Income Taxes Paid, net</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Income tax payments were $16.7 million in 2005, $39.6 million in 2004 and $10 million in 2003.
</P>

<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U>NOTE 11: &nbsp;CAPITAL STOCK</U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Common stock and class B common stock have the same dividend and liquidation rights. &nbsp;Class B common stock has ten votes per share, free convertibility into common stock on a one-for-one basis and can be transferred in class B form only to members of the stockholder&#146;s family and certain others affiliated with the stockholder. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company repurchased 0.6 million shares in early 2003 for $19.8 million at an average cost of $35.72 per share. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005, approximately $326.4 million remained under board authorization for share repurchases.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:4.15pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:4.15pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>On April 20, 2005 the Company's shareholders approved an amendment to the Company's bylaws and certificate of incorporation reducing the threshold at which shares of class B common stock are automatically converted into shares of common stock from 12,000,000 to 7,500,000 shares. </P>

<P style="page-break-before:always; margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Share-Based Compensation Plans</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Dow Jones 2001 Long-Term Incentive Plan (the plan) provides for the grant of contingent stock rights, stock options, restricted stock, restricted stock units and other stock-based awards (collectively, &#147;plan awards&#148;). &nbsp;At the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, an amendment to the plan was approved which increased the number of shares issuable under the plan by 1,500,000 shares to 10,500,000 shares. The Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors administers the plan. &nbsp;Under the plan, common stock may be granted for plan awards through March 31, 2011. &nbsp;The plan was the successor to the Dow Jones 1997 Long-Term Incentive Plan, which provided benefits to key senior executives, and the Dow Jones 1998 Stock Option Plan, which primarily provided benefits for middle management. &nbsp;At December 31, 2005, there were approximately 3.9 million shares available for future grants under the 2001 plan. &nbsp;Shares that remained under 1998 plan have been retired.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Stock options</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Options for shares of common stock may be granted under existing plans at not less than the fair market value of the common stock on the date of grant. &nbsp;In December 2004, under authorization of the Board of Directors, the Company accelerated the vesting of all unvested options granted after 2002. &nbsp;Accordingly, all options outstanding at December 31, 2005 were exercisable other than the 2005 grants. &nbsp;Stock options granted subsequent to December 31, 2004 will vest and become exercisable three years from the date of grant pursuant to the new three-year cliff vesting schedule. &nbsp;Options expire 10 years from the date of grant.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Contingent stock rights</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Contingent stock rights, granted under the Long-Term Incentive Plan, entitle the participant to receive future payments in the form of common stock, cash or a combination of both. &nbsp;The compensation ultimately received will depend on the extent to which specific performance criteria are achieved during the respective performance period (three years for 2005 and 2004 grants; four years for prior grants), the participant&#146;s individual performance and other factors, as determined by the compensation committee. &nbsp;Compensation received could be less than or equal to that specified in the right, but cannot exceed the right.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Restricted stock units and Restricted stock awards</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Restricted stock units cliff vest at the end of three years from the date of grant and are payable in the Company&#146;s common stock. &nbsp;Any dividends accrued during this period would be payable at the end of the three year period in cash. &nbsp;In 2005, 220,000 shares of restricted stock units were granted at $40.67 per share. &nbsp;In 2004, 101,000 shares of restricted stock units were granted at $52.65 per share. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005 28,000 shares had lapsed which comprised of 14,000 shares from each of the 2005 and 2004 awards.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The vesting of restricted stock awards may be conditional upon the completion of a specified period of employment, upon attainment of specified performance goals, and/or any other such criteria as the Compensation Committee may determine. &nbsp;In 2005, 34,000 shares of restricted stock were granted at a market value of $1.2 million. &nbsp;In 2003, 6,900 shares of restricted stock were granted at a market value of $0.3 million.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><I>Stock purchase plan</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Under the terms of the Dow Jones 1998 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, eligible employees may purchase shares of the Company&#146;s common stock based on compensation through payroll deductions or lump-sum payment. &nbsp;The purchase price for payroll deductions is the lower of 85% of the fair market value of the stock on the first or last day of the purchase period. &nbsp;Lump-sum purchases are made during the offering period at the lower of 85% of the fair market value of the stock on the first day of the purchase period or the payment date. &nbsp;At December 31, 2005, there were 1,047,000 shares available for future offerings. &nbsp;Under the plan, the Company sold 104,000 shares, 109,000 shares, and 105,000 shares to employees in 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><BR></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U>NOTE 13: &nbsp;BUSINESS SEGMENTS</U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company reports the results of its operations in three segments: print publishing, electronic publishing and community newspapers. &nbsp;In addition, the Company reports certain administrative activities under corporate. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Print publishing, which is largely comprised of the global editions of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I>, publishes business and financial content worldwide. &nbsp;This content is published primarily in the U.S., Europe, Asia and Latin America editions of <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> and on U.S. television through a licensing arrangement with CNBC. &nbsp;The Company manages the global Journal operations as one segment as their products comprise the global Journal brand, and there are significant interrelationships within the editions including global management, shared news flows and workforce and a global advertising customer base, sales force and pricing. &nbsp;U.S. television, which represents a licensing agreement with NBC Universal to provide branding, news content and on-air expertise to CNBC, is a further extension of the Journal brand and content. &nbsp;The Company also includes the operations of <I>Barron&#146;s</I> within print publishing instead of reporting them separately because of their relative immateriality to the Company&#146;s results on a consolidated basis and because <I>Barron&#146;s</I> shares services with and its operations are similar to the global Journal. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Electronic publishing, which electronically distributes business and financial news and information, includes the operations of Dow Jones Newswires, Consumer Electronic Publishing and Dow Jones Indexes/Ventures. &nbsp;Consumer Electronic Publishing includes the results of <I>WSJ.com</I> and its related vertical sites, MarketWatch and the Company&#146;s licensing/business development and radio/audio businesses. &nbsp;The Company manages electronic publishing as one segment, based on the similar distribution channels, global management, shared workforce and corporate branding. &nbsp;Revenues in the electronic publishing segment are mainly subscription-based. &nbsp;The community newspapers segment publishes 15 daily newspapers, 12 Sunday papers and more than 30 weekly newspapers and &#147;shoppers&#148; in nine states in the U.S. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:48.25pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:563.75pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>71</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Fair Value of Financial Instruments</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company&#146;s investments include marketable equity securities, which are carried at their market value. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005 the market value of these securities was $5.1 million reflecting an unrealized gain of $2.6 million. &nbsp;The remaining other investments are carried at original cost. &nbsp;</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>As of December 31, 2004, the market value of these securities was $7.4 million reflecting an unrealized gain of $4.9 million. &nbsp;The balance of the other investments is carried at original cost.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>These contracts, which expire over the subsequent year, are designated as cash flow hedges of anticipated operating expenses that are denominated in these foreign currencies. &nbsp;Revenues of the Company are largely collected in U.S. dollars. &nbsp;These contracts are entered into to mitigate foreign exchange volatility relative to these currencies. &nbsp;Realized gains or losses on foreign currency forward contracts are recognized currently through income and generally offset the transaction gains or losses on the foreign currency cash flows which they are intended to hedge. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The fair value of the contracts for year ended 2005 and 2004 was an unrealized loss of $0.3 million and an unrealized gain of $0.3 million, respectively. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>The Company also enters into foreign currency exchange forward contracts to limit the cash flow and earnings volatility that results from remeasuring certain foreign currency payables at prevailing exchange rates. &nbsp;The unrealized gains or losses of these forward contracts are recognized in Other, net in the income statement. &nbsp;The forward contract acts as an economic hedge by increasing in value when the underlying foreign currency payable decreases in value and conversely decreases in value when the underlying foreign currency payable increases. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005, the Company had forward currency exchange contracts outstanding to exchange 10 million British Pounds for $17.2 million, which are due to expire in the first quarter of 2006. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2004, the Company had forward currency exchange contracts outstanding to exchange 11 million British Pounds for $21.1 million, which expired in the first quarter of 2005.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B>Concentrations of Credit Risk</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Financial instruments that potentially could subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist largely of trade accounts receivable. &nbsp;The Company sells print and electronic information products world-wide to a wide variety of customers in the financial, business and private investor marketplaces. &nbsp;The concentration of credit risk with respect to trade receivables is slight due to the large number and geographic dispersion of customers that comprise the Company&#146;s customer base.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><B><U>NOTE 16: &nbsp;SUBSEQUENT EVENT</U></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Effective February 22, 2006, the Company established a new organizational structure pursuant to which it will organize and report its business around its three markets: &nbsp;consumer media, enterprise media, and community media. &nbsp;The Consumer Media Group will include <I>The Wall Street Journal</I> Franchise (including domestic and international print, online, television and radio); <I>Barron&#146;s</I> Franchise (including print, online and conferences); and, MarketWatch Franchise (including online, newsletters, television and radio). &nbsp;The Enterprise Media Group will include Dow Jones Newswires, Dow Jones Licensing Services, Dow Jones Indexes, Dow Jones Financial Information Services, and Dow Jones Reprints and Permissions. &nbsp;The Community Media Group will include the Company&#146;s portfolio of Ottaway community newspaper properties. &nbsp;In the first quarter of 2006 the Company expects to record employee severance and other charges related to the elimination of approximately 20 net positions. </P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><U>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</U></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>We have established disclosure controls and procedures to ensure that material information relating to the Company and its consolidated subsidiaries is made known to the officers who certify the Company&#146;s financial reports and to other members of senior management and the Board of Directors.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>Based on their evaluation as of December 31, 2005, the principal executive officer and principal financial officer of the Company have concluded that the Company&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures, as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act), are effective to ensure that the information required to be disclosed by the Company in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in SEC rules and forms. &nbsp;The information required to be disclosed by the Company in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to the Company&#146;s management, including the principal executive officer and principal financial officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><U>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</U></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:36pt; margin-bottom:0pt; width:576pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify>There were no changes in the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the three month period ended December 31, 2005 that have materially affected, or are reasonable likely to materially affect, the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting.</P>
